value.gap_vs_onpoint: GAP: Kilimall delivers a broad, price‑driven marketplace with local payment rails and a standard catalogue PDP, but it does not expose a user-facing, transparent fit/visualization workflow. There is no explicit “actual garment on me” render, nor any visible “similar look” approximation, nor a machine‑consumable supply graph for agent-enabled purchase. The blocker surfaces occur before any try-on or photo-upload flow could be engaged, implying a missing execution layer that OnPoint requires to connect fashion intent with real stock and local pay via an API/agent surface.

value.value_proposition: Kilimall presents an affordable, broad African marketplace with local payment rails and delivery; first-visit experience focuses on catalog breadth and deals rather than fit certainty or on‑person garment visualization.
value.what_onpoint_should_copy: Copy Kilimall’s strength in local payments and trust signals (Mpesa, wallet, card rails, delivery tracking, seller trust). Then differentiate with a visible, fit‑aware supply graph and explicit attribution of stock by size/color, plus an explicit “exact-SKU render on person” vs “inspiration only” label when a visualization exists. Publish a machine‑readable surface (OpenAPI/agent manifest) for inventory, stock, reserve, quote, and checkout intents, and integrate WhatsApp/M-Pesa handoff for a seamless agent‑addressable purchase.
